title: Wave 3 design: region emission from density-based fractals
description: fern, ifs, attractor, clifford, dejong, lorenz produce point clouds / density maps, not clean interior masks. Design question: how does the user specify the 'region' threshold? Options: (a) --density-percentile 80 (top 20% density cells are the region), (b) --min-points N (cells with at least N hits are in), (c) auto-threshold via Otsu on the density histogram. Pick one, document, implement once. Wave 3 implementation follows.

title: Evaluate SSIM/LPIPS as complement to gemma4 scoring
description: Gemma4 vision scoring plateaued at 8/6/7/7 across radically different SVG rendering approaches this session (pure vector, opacity blending, hi-res, hybrid raster-bg, SVG glow filter). Visual inspection shows real differences the model can't resolve. Add SSIM (structural similarity) and LPIPS (learned perceptual) metrics to scripts/fractal_qa.py so we have a quantitative tuning signal that tracks human perception better than gemma4.

title: Tune dragon julia preset — banding score 3/10
description: In the final QA sweep, dragon julia (cx=-0.8, cy=0.156) scored SVG-vs-raster banding of 3/10 while spiral and dendrite scored 6/10. Likely the c-value produces a highly fractal boundary that under-samples at the current resolution/level combination. Try higher resolution (1500+), higher level count (80+), or tighter geomspace range around the body boundary. Reproduce with: `python scripts/fractal_qa.py --preset dragon --target ../vpype-raster/examples/julia_dragon.jpg`

title: Principled banding fix: SVG <linearGradient> between adjacent contours
description: Current fill stacking produces visible banding even with opacity blending. True smooth gradient requires per-contour-pair linearGradient defs in SVG. Each annular region between contour_i and contour_{i+1} gets its own gradient interpolating their colors. Substantially larger refactor than svg_fill text-post-processing; requires geometric reasoning about which contour encloses which. Only worth doing if pixel-perfect SVG-vs-raster parity becomes a hard requirement. For now hybrid mode (--bg) achieves visual parity by embedding the raster.

description: Unlike other 1D L-system curves, the Koch island encloses an area. If a user requests it, emit the closed-region mask via marching squares on the path's filled silhouette. Low priority — only if the need comes up.

title: Add --emit-region to mandelbrot command (pilot for ADR-001)
description: Pilot implementation of the cross-plugin region-producer protocol (ADR-001). When --emit-region is passed, mandelbrot writes a boolean mask (interior=True, exterior=False) to the shared region-set metadata key instead of (or with --also-lines, alongside) emitting lines. Threshold is the escape-time field: iterations == max_iter means interior. Reuses --width/--height/--bounds for resolution. First real test of the protocol — expect to refine the contract based on this work.
notes: Shipped 2026-04-14. Pilot complete via shared _region.emit_region_mask helper. Verified end-to-end.

title: Wave 2c: region-aware mode for julia/mandelbrot (fractals inside fractals)
description:
Julia/Mandelbrot inside Julia/Mandelbrot regions — the most recursive case. Use the region bounds from get_region_context to set --x-min/--x-max/--y-min/--y-max automatically instead of requiring explicit flags. Clip escape-time contour output to the region mask (marching squares already operates on a 2D field; just masking it before extraction would work).

Aesthetic goal: a Julia spiral whose interior is filled with a smaller Mandelbrot. Or a Mandelbrot whose interior is filled with Julia contours at varying c-values per region. This is the payoff for the whole region-producer protocol.

title: Wave 2b: region-aware mode for geometric fractals (carpet, sierpinski, dragon, koch)
description:
Currently only space-filling curves (hilbert, gosper, peano) read the current region mask in forregion. To unlock the full 'fractals within fractals' story, the geometric and L-system fractals need the same treatment:

- carpet, sierpinski, sierpinski-triangle — clip their output to the region mask
- dragon, koch, koch-island, levy, minkowski, tree, lsystem — clip 1D paths to the region mask

Shared helper: vpype_fractal._region.get_region_context already provides the bounds + mask. What's missing is: (1) consult it for bounds (replace hardcoded output size), (2) clip geometry to the mask (likely via vpype's linemask-style boolean op or shapely intersection).

See examples/region_fractal/NESTED.md in vpype-raster for the working cases and the 'not yet supported' note.

title: Reduce gradient banding in julia/mandelbrot SVG output
description:
Gemma4 validation consistently scores 'banding: 7/10' on SVG-rasterized output — discrete iso-level fills produce visible bands where the raster has smooth gradient. Options: (a) bump default --levels from 20 to 60, (b) use linear instead of geomspace distribution in the far-exterior range, (c) add a gradient-fill SVG mode using <linearGradient> between adjacent contours. (a) is cheapest; (c) is the principled fix.

Scoring harness is at scripts/fractal_qa.py. Run: `python scripts/fractal_qa.py --preset spiral --target ../vpype-raster/examples/julia_spiral.jpg`
notes:
Session 2026-04-13 progress: level distribution switched to hybrid linear+geomspace; default levels 20→60; fill-opacity option added to svg_fill.py (body fill stays solid, only gradient bands get alpha-blended). Best result so far (dendrite): SVG-vs-target fidelity=9, gradient=7. Banding remains visible on grayscale palette (color masks bands better). Next candidate: SVG <linearGradient> between adjacent contour pairs for principled smoothness.
Iter 5 (2026-04-13): Hybrid mode (raster bg + stroke overlay) tested quantitatively via SSIM. Results: spiral 0.79, dendrite 0.90, dragon 0.81 (svg-vs-raster). That's 6x better than filled mode (0.13-0.14). Hybrid now canonical default in QA harness for 'SVG matches PNG' requirement. Pure-vector mode for plotting still needs principled linearGradient approach if users require pure SVG visual parity.
Iter 6 (2026-04-13) RESOLVED for pure-vector: added radialGradient-per-band mode (svg_fill.py --radial). Each annular region between adjacent contours fills with a radialGradient from this band's color to the next, anchored at viewbox centroid. Body stays solid black. SSIM svg-vs-raster improves from filled's 0.14 to radial's 0.14-0.19 (marginal on metric, strong on perceived smoothness — no more discrete band steps). Closing as resolved: hybrid for visual parity, radial for plot-compatible smoothness, filled/pure for legacy.
